```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)

library(haven) # to read .XPT files 
library(dplyr) # data manipulation
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(car)

```

## R Load Data
```{r load_data, include=TRUE}

# 11 files from NHANES that we want - has our predictors & outcome 
files <- c("DEMO_J", "GLU_J", "BMX_J", "BPX_J", "DIQ_J",
           "HDL_J", "TRIGLY_J", "INS_J", "ALQ_J", "PAQ_J", "SMQ_J")

# web address for 2017-2018 nhanes data 
base <- "https://wwwn.cdc.gov/Nchs/Data/Nhanes/Public/2017/DataFiles/"

# for each name in files (above) - download 
tables <- map(files, function(f) {
  tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".xpt")
  download.file(paste0(base, f, ".XPT"), tmp, mode = "wb")
  
  # turn downloaded file into readable table
  read_xpt(tmp)
  
})

# label each of 11 tables with file name for later use 
names(tables) <- files

```

## Current list of data files

DEMO_J = demographic data
BPX_J = blood pressure
BMX_J = body measurements
GLU_J = plasma fasting glucose 
HDL_J = Cholesterol - High - Density Lipoprotein (HDL)
TRIGLY_J = Cholesterol - Low-Density Lipoproteins (LDL) & Triglycerides
INS_J = insulin 
DIQ_J = diabetes 
ALQ_J = alcohol use 
PAQ_J = physical activity 
SMQ_J - cigarette use 

```{r select_rows, include=TRUE}

# join 11 tables from data load into one large table called nhanes - match on SEQN (participant ID)
nhanes <- reduce(tables, left_join, by = "SEQN")

# will be number of people in demographics file (first table)
cat("Rows after merge:", nrow(nhanes), "\n")

# narrow down to columns of interest 
nhanes_small <- nhanes %>%
  select(SEQN,                          # participant ID
         glucose = LBXGLU,              # fasting glucose (outcome)
         age = RIDAGEYR,                # age
         sex_code = RIAGENDR,           # sex
         pregnant = RIDEXPRG,           # pregnancy (filter only)
         bmi = BMXBMI,                  # BMI
         sys_bp1 = BPXSY1,              # systolic BP readings (to average)
         sys_bp2 = BPXSY2,              # systolic BP readings (to average)
         sys_bp3 = BPXSY3,              # systolic BP readings (to average)
         hdl = LBDHDD,                  # HDL
         triglycerides = LBXTR,         # triglycerides
         insulin = LBXIN,               # insulin (optional extra)
         dx_diabetes = DIQ010,          # diabetes diagnosis
         on_insulin = DIQ050,           # diabetes on insulin
         on_pills = DIQ070,             # diabetes on meds (filter only)
         smoked_100 = SMQ020,           # smoked 100+ cigarettes in life
         vigorous_rec = PAQ650,         # vigorous recreational activity 
         moderate_rec = PAQ665)         # moderate recreational activity

cat("Columns kept:", ncol(nhanes_small), "\n")

```


```{r filter_data, include=TRUE}

# keep adults (18+) who have a fasting glucose value
nhanes_fasting <- nhanes_small %>% filter(!is.na(glucose), age >= 18)
cat("Adults with fasting glucose:", nrow(nhanes_fasting), "\n")

# exclude pregnant women
nhanes_not_pregnant <- nhanes_fasting %>% filter(is.na(pregnant) | pregnant != 1)
cat("After excluding pregnant:", nrow(nhanes_not_pregnant), "\n")

# make data for model (from the one excluding pregnant women and only with fasting glucose adults)
nhanes_variables <- nhanes_not_pregnant %>%
  mutate(
    sex = factor(sex_code, levels = c(1, 2), labels = c("Male", "Female")), # categorical label for M/F
    sys_bp = rowMeans(select(., sys_bp1, sys_bp2, sys_bp3), na.rm = TRUE), # average 3 systolic BP
    sys_bp = ifelse(is.nan(sys_bp), NA, sys_bp),
    smoker = case_when(smoked_100 == 1 ~ 1, smoked_100 == 2 ~ 0), # give 1 if person smoked 100+ ciggs (0 other)
    active_rec = case_when(vigorous_rec == 1 | moderate_rec == 1 ~ 1, # give 1 if person does vigorous or moderate recreational activity (0 other)
                           vigorous_rec == 2 & moderate_rec == 2 ~ 0),
    diabetes_dx = if_else(dx_diabetes %in% 1 | on_insulin %in% 1 | on_pills %in% 1, 1, 0) # 1 if person told they have diabetes, takes meds for db
  )

# checks
table(nhanes_variables$diabetes_dx, useNA = "ifany")
table(nhanes_variables$smoker, useNA = "ifany")
table(nhanes_variables$active_rec, useNA = "ifany")
table(nhanes_variables$sex_code, nhanes_variables$sex)
summary(nhanes_variables$sys_bp)

head(nhanes_variables)
```
```{r missing_data, include=TRUE}

# count blanks in every column
colSums(is.na(nhanes_variables))

# columns the model needs: outcome + 8 predictors
core <- c("glucose", "age", "sex", "bmi", "sys_bp",
          "hdl", "triglycerides", "smoker", "active_rec")

# keep only people with no blanks in those columns
nhanes_model_data <- nhanes_variables %>% drop_na(all_of(core))
cat("Final modeling sample:", nrow(nhanes_model_data), "\n")

# save 
write.csv(nhanes_model_data, "nhanes_glucose_model.csv", row.names = FALSE)

# relabel as No/Yes for plots and models
nhanes_model_data$smoker <- factor(nhanes_model_data$smoker, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))
nhanes_model_data$active_rec <- factor(nhanes_model_data$active_rec, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("No", "Yes"))

head(nhanes_model_data)


```



```{r summary_statistics, include=TRUE}

model1 <- lm(log(glucose) ~ age + sex + bmi + sys_bp + hdl + log(triglycerides) + smoker + active_rec, data = nhanes_model_data)

summary(model1)

residualPlots(model1)

```
